beats.title: Remember the Ladies Letter
beats.description: Abigail Adams urged her husband to remember women when the new nation's laws were drawn up, or women would foment a rebellion.
beats.why_in: early precursor of the fight for women's political rights

beats.title: Declaration of the Rights of Woman
beats.description: A French playwright answered the revolution's declaration of rights by demanding the same civil and political rights for women.
beats.why_in: early demand for women's political equality

beats.title: Vindication of the Rights of Woman
beats.description: Mary Wollstonecraft published a landmark book arguing that women deserve education and a full place in public life.
beats.why_in: foundational text of the suffrage cause

beats.title: New Jersey Takes the Vote Back
beats.description: A state that had quietly let propertied women vote changed its law and limited the franchise to white men.
beats.why_in: early women's voting rights won and lost

beats.title: Women Turned Away in London
beats.description: Female delegates were refused seats at an anti-slavery convention, pushing two of them toward organising for women's rights.
beats.why_in: spark for the organised women's rights movement

beats.title: Seneca Falls Convention
beats.description: Hundreds gathered in a small New York town and adopted a Declaration of Sentiments demanding that women be given the vote.
beats.why_in: launch of the American suffrage movement

beats.title: National Women's Rights Convention
beats.description: Activists met in Massachusetts for the first nationwide gathering devoted to women's rights, including the vote.

beats.title: Ain't I a Woman Speech
beats.description: Sojourner Truth, a formerly enslaved woman, challenged a women's rights meeting in Ohio with a famous speech on race and gender.
beats.why_in: landmark speech in the women's rights movement

beats.title: Petition to Parliament for Women
beats.description: A petition with thousands of signatures was carried to the House of Commons asking that women householders be allowed to vote.

beats.title: Wyoming Women Get the Vote
beats.description: A western territory became the first place in the United States to give women full voting rights.

beats.title: Anthony Arrested for Voting
beats.description: A leading campaigner cast a ballot in a presidential election and was arrested and put on trial for it.
beats.why_in: act of defiance in the suffrage fight

beats.title: Anthony Amendment Introduced
beats.description: A proposed change to the US Constitution to guarantee women the vote was first put before Congress.

beats.title: Isle of Man Women Gain the Vote
beats.description: A small island parliament let propertied unmarried women and widows vote in general elections, ahead of nearly everywhere.

beats.title: American Suffrage Groups Merge
beats.description: Two rival women's suffrage organisations joined forces to form one national association to win the vote state by state.

beats.title: New Zealand Women Vote
beats.description: A self-governing colony became the first country in the world where women could vote in national elections.
beats.why_in: first nation to grant women the vote

beats.title: South Australia Lets Women Stand
beats.description: An Australian colony gave women both the vote and the right to run for parliament, a world first.

beats.title: Australian Women Win Federal Vote
beats.description: A new federal law gave most Australian women the right to vote and stand in national elections.

beats.title: Pankhurst Founds the Suffragettes
beats.description: Emmeline Pankhurst launched a Manchester organisation with the motto deeds, not words, to win votes for women.
beats.why_in: start of militant British suffrage campaign

beats.title: Finland Leads Europe
beats.description: Finnish women won the vote and the right to stand for parliament, a first in Europe.

beats.title: Emily Davison at the Derby
beats.description: A suffragette ran onto a racecourse in front of the King's horse and died of her injuries days later.

beats.title: Representation of the People Act
beats.description: British women over thirty who met property conditions won the vote after a long and bitter campaign.

beats.title: 19th Amendment Ratified
beats.description: The final state approved a constitutional change declaring that the vote could not be denied because of sex.

beats.title: Equal Franchise Act
beats.description: British women gained the vote on the same terms as men, lowering the age for women to twenty-one.
beats.why_in: equal voting age for women in Britain

beats.title: Spanish Women Gain the Vote
beats.description: The new Spanish republic's constitution gave women the vote after a fierce parliamentary debate.

beats.title: Turkey Grants Women the Vote
beats.description: Turkish women won full national voting and candidacy rights as part of the republic's sweeping reforms.

beats.title: French Women Win the Vote
beats.description: A provisional government's ordinance gave French women the vote, which they first used in local elections the next year.

beats.title: Argentina's Women's Suffrage Law
beats.description: Eva Perón campaigned for the law that gave Argentine women the vote, and it passed Congress.

beats.title: India Gives Women the Vote
beats.description: A new constitution gave all adult Indian citizens, women included, an equal vote from the start of the republic.
beats.why_in: universal suffrage including women in India

beats.title: Egyptian Women Vote
beats.description: A new constitution gave Egyptian women the right to vote and run for office.
beats.note: 1956 constitution and election law; first used in 1957

beats.title: Vaud Opens the Swiss Ballot
beats.description: A French-speaking Swiss canton became the first there to give women the vote, while the nation as a whole said no.

beats.title: Iranian Women Gain the Vote
beats.description: A package of reforms put to a referendum brought votes for Iranian women, drawing fierce opposition from clerics.
beats.note: Referendum January 1963; sources differ on the exact legal date

beats.title: Swiss Men Vote Yes for Women
beats.description: Swiss men approved a referendum giving women the federal vote, long after most of Europe.

beats.title: Liechtenstein Women Vote
beats.description: A close referendum of men gave women the vote in the last European country to do so nationally.

beats.title: Last Swiss Canton Forced to Comply
beats.description: The highest court ordered a small Alpine canton to let women vote in local affairs after its men kept refusing.
beats.why_in: last holdout for women's suffrage in Switzerland
beats.note: Court ruling November 1990; women voted there from 1991

beats.title: South African Women Vote Freely
beats.description: Women of every race voted in the country's first fully democratic election.
beats.why_in: universal suffrage for women in South Africa

beats.title: Kuwait Gives Women the Vote
beats.description: Kuwait's parliament passed a law granting women political rights after years of defeated proposals.

beats.title: UAE Women Vote for the First Time
beats.description: Emirati women took part in the country's first limited elections, both as voters and candidates.

beats.title: Saudi King Promises Women the Vote
beats.description: The ruler announced that women would be allowed to vote and stand in municipal elections in a few years.

beats.title: Saudi Women Vote and Run
beats.description: Women in Saudi Arabia voted and stood as candidates in local elections for the first time.
